text:
Elaine: Heads-up — want to sketch an 'opportunistic backstop' policy for mixed on-demand+spot pools. Goal: keep 95th percentile latency SLAs while maximizing spot usage. Thoughts?

Mike: +1. We need a hard min on-demand floor per AZ (e.g. 8-12% of capacity) and a fast fallback path for preemptions. If spot drop happens, shift new requests to on-demand, and drain existing spot jobs with a KV-cache-preserve handshake.

Anjali: Agree. Also propose progressive reclaim: when spot revocations spike, first route non-latency-critical batches to spot reclaim queue, then scale on-demand if reclaim queue grows > 3 min backlog. Keeps cost savings but avoids sudden SLA attacks.

DevBot: deploy-bot: autoscaler rule update applied to fleet-config/prod-mix: added fallback_threshold=0.6 and reclaim_queue_limit=180s :rocket:

Jules: For latency-sensitive routes (chat/generation) we should pin a separate small pool of pure on-demand or use instant-evict-safe models. Can we tag models/routes as "hard-sla" and have routing prefer on-demand?

Ryan: Cost perspective — with 85% spot target we save ~40% unit cost but risk 2-3% request reroutes during busy revocation windows. Proposed trade: maintain 10% on-demand + 5% burst capacity (pre-warmed on-demand) in top regions. Example config we ran locally:
```json
{"pool_policy":"mixed","min_on_demand_pct":10,"burst_on_demand_pct":5,"spot_target_pct":85,"fallback_latency_ms":200}
```
Small numbers, but gives predictable warm capacity for short spikes.

Jules: How are we handling KV cache warmups if we move users between model variants? Need quick cache resync or async warm path to avoid token regen penalties.

Anjali: Two ideas: async prefix warm (background warm threads copy hottest KV to on-demand instance) + ephemeral proxy that holds last-k cache entries during handoff. Adds complexity but reduces regen.

Mike: Operational playbook snippets:
- monitor: spot_revocations/min and reclaim_queue_seconds
- trigger: if revocations/min > 5 for 2m -> increase on-demand target by +20% or enable burst pool
- fallback: route NEW requests to on-demand, allow spot tasks to finish up to 30s, then preempt

ops-bot: alert: us-west-2 spot eviction surge at 1991233200 caused 3% throughput loss for 90s (see incident/1991233200). Auto-fallback prevented broader SLA breach.

Elaine: Nice. Action items: (1) Mike + Anjali draft a short ops playbook with thresholds and commands, (2) Ryan to run cost simulation for 5/10/15% min-on-demand across our top 3 regions, (3) Jules to prototype KV warm proxy. Sync tomorrow 11am.

Mike: I'll start playbook. quick command for debugging: `rkctl get-fleet --region us-west-2 --pool mixed -o wide` shows slot allocation by class.

Anjali: adding sample alarm rule: `expr: increase(spot_revocations_total[2m]) > 5` -> pager.

DevBot: reminder: PR #3124 (mixed-pool-fallback) awaiting review.

Elaine: Perfect — keep this thread updated with PR links and simulation outputs. :thumbsup:
